Is CEBRA the problem?

A controlled investigation of endpoint information, contrastive objectives, model capacity, cue time and synthetic population construction.

Read this before the scores. We predict inferred ordered (start, goal), not a navigation path. Evaluation rows are assembled using their known true condition from different sessions. This is conditional synthetic separability—not decoding one unknown real trial. Every new comparison uses an already inspected development set.
195 units58 session labels; fixed original panel
15,553 sources12,288 training / 3,265 development
25 settingsfixed-setting method screen, all reported
37.6 minsum of successful phase wall times; not just GPU kernels
AnswerData & designModelsResultsDiagnosisCE follow-upInside the modelsStudent comparisonScalingNullsResearch trailLimits & next stepsReproduce

1. The answer, at the right level of certainty

Do not conclude that CEBRA is intrinsically broken. A CEBRA synthetic positive control reached 100% on new draws of a strong condition signal; constant features produced exactly 3.33% chance. Real-data performance depends on the representation objective, information window, training duration and decoder—not just the method name.

At the common 3,000-update comparison, PCA8/bin scores 83.61%, legacy Behavior at τ=1 13.61%, time-matched Behavior at τ=.3 59.58%, whole-cue Behavior 30.56%, and the binwise cross-entropy encoder 20.00%. The descriptively highest screened setting is PCA: 8/bin → 80 (83.61%). This ranking is a development observation, not independent evidence of method superiority.

A key diagnostic result: matching positive examples by pair and cue bin, while retaining global negatives, reaches 83.33% at 250 updates—close to the PCA baseline. Its later checkpoints deteriorate. This implicates the original time-mixing objective and overtraining, rather than an inherent inability of CEBRA to represent endpoint information. This early checkpoint is now an inspected development result, not a newly selected confirmatory winner.

More importantly, good endpoint decoding does not answer the thesis question of path information beyond endpoints. The task here is a diagnostic stepping stone, not evidence for planning or H1.

2. What one example actually is

  1. A source is a real behavioral trial with a session identity. Its start is inferred from the preceding successful trial's marker; its goal from the current marker. These semantics are provisional.
  2. Only eligible original-training trials are used: successful current and preceding trials, sequential in the same session, required QC checks and a complete current cue of at least one second. The previous trial supplies a label, not spike features.
  3. Count spikes in ten half-open 100 ms bins from cue onset: [0,.1), …, [.9,1). A cell contributes ten counts.
  4. Split sources before assembly. For a condition such as 2→5, draw one matching source per session and retain that session's selected cells and all bins together.
  5. Concatenate the session blocks: one artificial example is 195 cells × 10 bins. Repeat 16 times/class for training (480 rows) and 8 times/class for development (240 rows), for three seeds. 
real sources ── source split ─┬─ training pools ── conditional assembly ── fit preprocessing/model/readout
                             └─ development pools ── conditional assembly ── transform and predict only
condition label ───────────────────────↑ selects matching components on BOTH sides

ML analogy: imagine a dataset assembled by taking one feature block from each of 58 documents known to have the same topic. You can measure topic information in the assembled vector, but it is not a classifier for one naturally occurring document. Cross-document co-occurrence is manufactured by construction.

The inner split is session-and-condition-stratified with frozen seed 20260907. All original validation/test features remain excluded. Same-source bins never cross this split. Success-conditioned eligibility, place-cell selection, previous/current label dependence and session drift are still possible sources of bias.

Three distinct sample counts: 195 units are channels; 15,553 source trials are recorded observations across sessions; 480/240 pseudorows are synthetic recombinations. None of these equals 480 independent simultaneous-population trials.

Plain-English learning notes · 13 September 2026

Added after the original study to explain this report. These notes and the two new plots reuse saved exploratory results; no models were retrained. The original study text, nine figures and metric download remain unchanged.

The question here: can cue-period neural activity distinguish a condition such as start at 2, go to 5 from other start–goal combinations? This is not yet a test of which path the animal takes between those endpoints.

Jump to: one example · PCA 8/bin → 80 · what C means · CEBRA-Time and plots · interpretability.

1. One example, in ordinary language

  1. A source is one real trial. Its session tells us which recording session it came from. If the previous successful trial ended at 2 and the current marker indicates goal 5, the analysis labels the current trial 2→5. This interpretation of the markers remains provisional, not independently verified task meaning.
  2. Keep only eligible trials. The current and immediately preceding trials must both be successful and sequential in the same session; the current trial must pass the required quality checks and provide at least one complete second of cue activity. The previous trial supplies the inferred start label, not neural input features.
  3. Turn spike timestamps into counts. A spike is a recorded firing event. Divide the first cue second into ten 100 ms windows and count each cell’s spikes in each window. One cell might give [0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 1, 0, 0, 2, 1]. A spike exactly at 100 ms goes into the second window, not both.
  4. Split the real trials first. Put each source into training or development before making artificial combinations. Otherwise, different combinations on both sides could contain pieces of the same real trial. Keeping one source’s bins together does not remove all dependence between neighboring trials.
  5. Assemble one artificial population. For a 2→5 example, choose one matching trial per session, keep that session’s selected cells and all ten bins together, then join the session blocks. The result has 195 cells × 10 bins = 1,950 counts. Those cells were spread across sessions; this is not one verified simultaneous 195-cell trial. 
Session A: cells from one real 2→5 trial ─┐
Session B: cells from one real 2→5 trial ─┼─ join → one artificial 195 × 10 example
Session C and other sessions: likewise ─┘

There are 30 ordered endpoint classes. Making 16 examples per class gives 480 training rows; making eight gives 240 development rows. Three seeds mean three randomized repetitions, not three new biological datasets. Reusing sources within a pool makes more combinations, not more recorded observations.

The crucial limitation: the true endpoint label chooses matching components on both sides of the split. The classifier is not directly handed the answer as a feature, but the answer helped construct its input. We measure how distinguishable these known-condition artificial populations are—not performance on one naturally recorded, unknown trial. “No source overlap” is necessary, but does not make this an ordinary deployment benchmark.

2. What does “PCA: 8/bin → 80” mean?

Compress the cell dimension separately at each time window, then keep all ten windows. Each of the eight PCA values is a weighted combination of the standardized 195 cell counts, not one selected cell. PCA finds directions of high variation in training data; it does not use endpoint labels to choose those directions directly. 

Each 100 ms bin: 195 counts → shared PCA transformation → 8 values
Whole cue:      [bin 1’s 8 | bin 2’s 8 | … | bin 10’s 8]
                                       ↓
                             80 classifier features

The code fits one shared StandardScaler + PCA on the pooled training-bin vectors and applies that same transformation to every training and development bin. It does not fit ten separate PCAs. This is an 80-feature whole-cue representation, not an eight-dimensional whole-cue representation. The separate “whole cue → 8” recipe compresses all 1,950 counts into just eight values.

3. What does C = 0.1 mean? Why does this report use C = 0.01? 

Spike counts → PCA or CEBRA → 80 features → logistic classifier → endpoint pair
                                                  ↑
                                             C acts here

C controls the final classifier’s regularization. The classifier learns weights telling it how strongly each feature should affect a prediction. The L2 penalty discourages large weights: “Do not make a huge decision from one shaky clue.” It shrinks weights rather than selecting a fixed number of features.

C Relative penalty strength, everything else fixed
1 Weaker regularization; the original baseline’s value.
0.1 Ten times stronger than C = 1.
0.01 Ten times stronger than C = 0.1; the common readout used in the new comparisons and plots.

Smaller C means stronger regularization because the penalty strength scales inversely with C. Too little can encourage fitting noise; too much can suppress useful signal. C = 0.01 was chosen from an earlier development diagnosis, not established as a universally optimal value. Changing C changes the readout, not the already-trained encoder.

Do not confuse C with CEBRA’s temperature τ, which scales similarities inside its contrastive loss, or with the weight decay used when training the separate cross-entropy neural-network control. They are different settings in different stages.

4. Which CEBRA-Time performed best?

Actual CEBRA-Time reached its highest recorded three-seed mean here at 250 updates: 69.72% joint development accuracy. “Joint” means both start and goal are correct. There are 30 classes, so uniform chance is 3.33%. An update is an optimizer step, not a millisecond of brain activity and not a complete pass through the dataset.

CEBRA-Time chooses a positive pair from neighboring bins within the same artificial trial: for example, cue bin 3 and cue bin 4. Negatives are randomly sampled training bins. Its objective is roughly “make neighboring moments more similar than random comparisons.” Random negatives are not guaranteed to have a different endpoint label. 

One bin: 195 standardized counts → 32 → 32 → 16 → 8 → unit-length normalization
Ten bins: concatenate ten 8-value embeddings → 80 features → classifier, C = 0.01

The shared encoder sees one bin at a time; it is not an RNN or attention model reading the whole cue. “Time” describes how training pairs are selected. Endpoint labels are not supplied directly to this encoder’s learning objective, but they still determine the artificial example assembly and train the final classifier. The complete pipeline is therefore not label-free.

“Time-matched Behavior” is a different model. It chooses positives with the same endpoint pair and the same cue bin. For example, a 2→5 example at bin 3 is matched to another same-condition bin-3 example, rather than to bin 4 of itself. The matching pool permits self positives. The fully time-matched version also restricts negative comparisons to the reference bin.

Recipe 250 updates 1,000 updates 3,000 updates
CEBRA-Time, τ = 1 69.72% 51.67% 38.06%
Same pair + same-bin positives; global negatives, τ = 0.3 83.33% 75.00% 64.86%
Time-matched Behavior: positives and negatives matched to bin, τ = 0.3 81.94% 75.83% 59.58%
PCA 8/bin → 80 reference 83.61%; PCA has no iterative encoder-update schedule.

For the cleaner positive-sampling contrast at the same τ = 0.3 and 250 updates, the report records 53.06% for time-mixed Behavior versus 83.33% for same-bin positives with global negatives. The fully time-matched version also changes reference batching; use the grouped-reference bridge in §5 before attributing a difference solely to negative time matching.

5. What did the interpretability part actually tell us?

Deterministic means repeatable for fixed inputs and a fixed computation. Mechanistic interpretability means explaining how a model computes something. The report’s “Inside the models” section primarily performs representation diagnostics: it asks what information a simple classifier can read from intermediate features. It does not fully reverse-engineer the encoder or explain a biological planning circuit.

A linear probe is a small classifier attached to a frozen layer. Like probing an intermediate transformer layer for sentiment, it tests whether a target is accessible there. Fit the probe on training activations and evaluate on development activations; do not retrain the encoder. Hidden model coordinates are artificial features, not biological neurons.

At 10,000 updates, the first hidden-layer probe scored 57.36% for original Behavior and 66.39% for time-matched Behavior. Final normalized-output probes scored 19.72% and 41.81%. However, the first layer supplies 320 whole-cue features and the final layer only 80. Earlier layers being easier to decode does not prove information was destroyed later: feature count, nonlinear coding and finite-sample regularization also matter. These are late Behavior diagnostics, not probes of the best 250-update CEBRA-Time checkpoint.

Normalization removes vector length. Think of an embedding as an arrow with direction and length. [1, 2] and [3, 6] point the same way; unit normalization turns them into the same vector. Comparing before and after normalization keeps the feature count fixed. Original Behavior changed from 21.67% before to 19.72% after; time-matched Behavior changed from 39.03% to 41.81%. Removing length is not a consistent explanation for the large performance gap.

Participation ratio summarizes how widely variance spreads. A point cloud shaped like a line mainly varies along one direction; a sheet mainly varies along two. At 10,000 updates the ratio was 3.73 out of 8 for original Behavior and 7.67 out of 8 for time-matched Behavior. This is an effective spread of variance, not a count of represented classes, a measure of mutual information, or proof of named biological axes. Noise can fill dimensions too.

Take-home: simple PCA was a strong endpoint reference; sampling choices and training duration mattered for these CEBRA recipes. None of these plots establishes path information beyond endpoints, the exact state of a simultaneous population, intention, or a planning mechanism.

3. The models in ML terms

PCA versus CEBRA versus a classifier

  • PCA learns high-variance linear directions after train-only count standardization. Here eight dimensions are learned from single-bin 195-vectors, then ten embeddings are concatenated into 80 readout features. This is not an eight-dimensional whole-trial representation.
  • CEBRA learns a nonlinear metric from positive/negative sampling. Its original encoder is 195 → 32 → 32 → 16 → 8, GELU nonlinearities, then unit normalization: 7,992 parameters. It sees one bin at a time, not a recurrent sequence or attention window.
  • Contrastive objective: increase similarity to sampled positives relative to negatives. CEBRA's installed cosine criterion uses −similarity(ref,pos)/τ + logsumexp(similarity(ref,negatives)/τ). Which examples count as positives determines what should be invariant.
  • Time positives are the next cue bin within the same pseudotrial. Behavior positives share the pair label but may come from different cue bins. “Same class” is not automatically “same latent state.”
  • Cross-entropy control uses the same binwise encoder but a 30-way linear head on the concatenated whole cue. It asks the network to classify the complete example, not to make every bin look like every same-label bin. Its loss granularity, batch size and additional head parameters differ; this is a capability control, not an isolated loss-only experiment.
  • Whole-cue controls flatten all 1,950 counts first, then learn an eight-dimensional representation. They change input context, parameter count and readout dimension. Report them separately from strict binwise ablations.

The new common learned-representation readout is train-fitted StandardScaler + multinomial logistic regression, C=.01. This was chosen from the previous development diagnosis, not independently preregistered. LDA, shrinkage LDA, PLS8 and RBF SVM are fixed comparator recipes, not exhaustively tuned families.

Why not immediately try LFADS or GPFA?

The present data do not establish simultaneous cross-session population activity. Models designed to infer single-trial population dynamics would invite an interpretation unsupported by the observation design. First test simple condition decoders and the concrete CEBRA mismatches.

A rising training-readout score with a falling development-readout score is overfitting of the combined representation/readout pipeline. Declining InfoNCE while endpoint decoding worsens shows that progress on the training objective is not progress on this generalization question. It does not by itself prove that every neuron feature is memorized or that CEBRA cannot work elsewhere.

Sampler precision matters: CEBRA contrasts every reference with every negative, a B×B matrix. Matching only each reference's paired negative would leave the denominator time-mixed. The matched variant draws one bin per reference batch; the grouped-reference/global-negative bridge separates batching from negative conditioning. Self positives and same-label negatives remain permitted, as in the legacy sampler; narrowing the positive pool also changes its self-match rate.

Temperature scales similarity logits and hence gradients and neighborhood pressure; lower is not universally better. Width changes network capacity. Latent dimension also changes the final readout feature count and, in this stock offset1 architecture, the preceding hidden layer (16 → 32 when output8 → 16). It is not a pure output-width-only intervention. A common regularizer is fair as a fixed recipe, but not equal effective complexity across dimensions.

5b. Was the supervised MLP also trained too long?

The poor 3,000-update CE endpoint was not enough to reject supervised networks. At 128 complete examples/update and 480 training rows, that is about 800 passes through the artificial training set. CEBRA instead samples reference bins plus positives/negatives; equal updates are not equal exposure. The one allowed adaptive follow-up therefore replayed both CE input windows, increased binwise weight decay from .001 to .1, and tested the already saved 64-pseudorows/class assembly. No further neural fit expansion followed.

These results distinguish early training from final-checkpoint performance. The common fixed readout and the actual trained head are both retained; neither is selected separately per configuration. Larger synthetic assemblies simultaneously reduce repeats per artificial example and increase use of the fixed recorded source pool. These curves are diagnostics, not independently validated hyperparameters.

Follow-up outcome: earlier checkpoints only modestly improved binwise CE; more recombinations helped substantially but did not close the PCA gap. Weight decay0.1 over-regularized this recipe to chance. The simple explanation “CE only needed early stopping or much stronger regularization” was insufficient here. Moderate regularization and other architectures remain untested; these results do not reject supervised neural networks as a family.

A hidden-layer probe is analogous to linear probing a transformer's intermediate residual stream. It asks: can a new linear readout extract the target from these coordinates on development examples? It does not tell us what a biological neuron “means.” Earlier layers have different feature budgets, so a higher score alone is not a controlled localization of information loss.

The pre-normalization versus normalized comparison is sharper: both have eight coordinates per bin. Unit normalization retains direction but removes vector length. If the pre-norm probe works better, useful linear-readout information may reside in that radial degree of freedom or the resulting geometry. Coordinate standardization and finite-sample regularization still influence this contrast. Here pre-norm probing improves legacy Behavior only slightly and worsens the time-matched encoder, so final unit normalization alone does not explain the large gap.

Spectral concentration is summarized by the participation ratio, 1/Σp² for normalized variance eigenvalues p. A ratio near three means variance is concentrated in roughly three directions—not “only three classes are represented,” not mutual information, and not proof of total collapse. Learned coordinates can rotate between seeds, so dimensions are not named biological axes.

The separate-goal LDA mean peaks descriptively at 0.4–0.5 s (81.25%). This is a six-class, single-bin result. It cannot be compared directly with a 30-class joint score or an 80-feature whole-cue decoder.

What was matched: our 195 cells, identical source splits, identical pseudo arrays and cue bins, with separately fitted start, goal and joint LDA. The modern factorized comparator multiplies separate start/goal probabilities and renormalizes over the 30 valid unequal pairs; it is not the student's heuristic collision repair.

What was not replicated: the student's exact historical cell selection (reported 233), preprocessing artifacts, bootstrap history and ten-fold evaluation. Those inputs/results were not recovered. In the public notebook at the audited commit, pooled-time-bin cell 70 uses row-index folds that can put bins of one trial on both sides. That concrete leakage finding does not invalidate every separate per-bin historical analysis by association.

The later-cue goal profile is compatible with current-cue sensory/task information. The early start profile may include previous-goal/location/history information. Neither pattern establishes prospective planning, a navigated path, or causal memory mechanisms.

Temporal-order sensitivity

A strict 75/25 session chronology has complete 30-class support in 1/58 sessions. The fixed 195-unit panel therefore does not support this exact strict-block construction. No outcome-driven session/condition selection was used to rescue it.

Split sensitivity Representation Joint development
reference pca_bin8 83.61%
reference matched_bin_t03 59.58%
chronological pca_bin8 87.78%
chronological matched_bin_t03 55.28%

Inspected development set · true-label-conditioned pseudopopulations · three assembly/training seeds · not independent biological replicates

The executed chronological sensitivity instead preserves each session/condition's original training/development counts and assigns earlier sources to training. It is not globally time-separated across conditions, not a new untouched holdout, and does not resolve serial dependence or generalization to new sessions.

Source sweep: nested fractions of inner-training sources with at least one source per session/condition; actual counts differ from the requested percentages. Unit sweep: nested random channels with identical source arrays before slicing; it also changes represented sessions and input-layer parameter count. Pseudorow sweep: more combinations of the same available source pool; it can expose more distinct available sources to the model without collecting any new biological data.

The 16-to-64-row/class change increases mean distinct training sources actually used from about 10,889 to 12,279, out of the same 12,288 available. Its gain therefore mixes broader use of existing recordings with recombination/optimization effects; it is not a pure synthetic-sample-count intervention. No new biological observations were collected.

These distinctions explain why additional synthetic rows can help optimization or population averaging without increasing evidence for a simultaneous circuit. Three seeds describe assembly and optimization sensitivity; they are not a source-aware confidence interval.

Inspected development set · true-label-conditioned pseudopopulations · three assembly/training seeds · not independent biological replicates

The fixed null panel was selected before the new real-data screen: PCA8/bin, time-matched τ=.3 CEBRA, and binwise CE, all three seeds. Labels are shuffled at source level before assembly and learned preprocessing. Shuffling existing pseudo-row labels after assembly would answer a different question and leave label-conditioned construction intact.

These five permutations are a falsification diagnostic. They are not a calibrated significance test, do not preserve trial-history dependence, and were not rerun for an adaptively chosen “winner.” Above-null performance only supports the limited conditional-assembly information claim.

10. The research trail: what changed, and why

  1. Observation: original CEBRA underperformed PCA; stronger decoder regularization helped partially. Working hypotheses were objective/sampling mismatch, optimization, bottleneck/normalization, and assembly limitations.
  2. Independent challenge before fitting: mechanism/literature, source-safety and methodological reviewers emphasized inspected-development status, label-conditioned evaluation, source reuse and time dependence. Added a temporal support audit and bounded sensitivity split.
  3. Implementation falsification: caught the all-to-all-negative sampler issue before fitting it. Added the bridge control and B×B sampler test, then checked synthetic signal, constant chance, normalization probes and old checkpoint parity.
  4. Checkpoint readout first: inspected original training trajectories with the common readout rather than assuming the last checkpoint is best. No encoder retraining was needed for that question.
  5. Fixed screen: ran simple alternatives, explicit sampler/temperature/capacity/context ablations and CE controls without validation early stopping. Retained every setting and every seed, not only favorable results.
  6. Source-aware sensitivity and falsification: separated source availability, channel count and recombination count; checked chronology and fully refitted the predeclared null panel.
  7. One adaptive follow-up: poor final CE performance prompted the four declared early-training/regularization/augmentation recipes, with exact replay checks and both readouts retained. These are separate from the fixed initial screen.
  8. Stopping rule: this is a bounded diagnostic study, not a search for a CEBRA setting that must win. Future tuning needs training-only/nested selection and a genuinely independent evaluation strategy; reusing these curves cannot manufacture one.

Initial static checking failed on third-party dynamic typing and array annotations before any new fit. Those receipts are retained. Narrow API annotation fixes and runtime dataset guards produced a clean typecheck; 12 tests and the synthetic controls passed. The independent implementation reviewer confirmed the sampler and source/target flows. Completed phase details:

Six CE replay fits also matched original final weights and predictions exactly. Fresh read-only artifact/content review returned no findings; this is not an independent biological replication.

The original checkout and original run artifacts were preserved. Work remains on baseline/start-goal-cebra in its isolated worktree. No original validation/test features were used and no persistent server was started.

11. What this does—and does not—teach us

Defensible conclusions

  • Endpoint condition information is accessible from this source-safe, cross-session assembly design.
  • The checkpoint, sampler, temperature, capacity, context and probe comparisons show how these specific recipes behave on an inspected development set.
  • A good neural embedding must be assessed against simpler alternatives on matched inputs, dimensions and evaluation—not only its training loss or visualization.

Still unresolved

  • No clean confirmatory ranking, p-value, animal/session generalization or source-aware interval follows from the three seeds. The original test also had earlier project exposure, although it was not used here.
  • Label-conditioned assembly is not unknown-real-trial deployment. Pseudopopulations cannot reconstruct simultaneous cross-session noise covariance.
  • Start/goal marker semantics and simultaneous recording metadata remain incompletely verified. Eligibility and place-cell selection limit generality.
  • Chronological-within-condition sensitivity is weaker than a strict contiguous-time or session-held-out evaluation. It cannot remove all serial/history confounding.
  • Linear probes measure accessible target information under their own regularization, not causal encoding or unique biological mechanisms.
  • The study does not predict actual paths, nor test path information conditional on start and goal. Goal decoding can reflect the displayed cue.

Recommended next move

  1. For a working endpoint baseline: retain the simple PCA/logistic recipe, with exact source-level provenance and a clearly named development endpoint. Do not replace it merely because a nonlinear method is more modern.
  2. For representation research: prioritize the matched contrasts above. Distinguish “CEBRA on whole examples” from forcing every local bin to identify a complete pair. Freeze selection rules inside training before another broad search.
  3. For the thesis: verify marker semantics and recording metadata, define actual path labels and their endpoint-conditioned alternatives, and establish a support-feasible independent evaluation. That changes the scientific question; higher endpoint accuracy alone does not advance H1.
